According to Bloomberg's latest report, Apple will launch a brand-new "Apple Upgrade" leasing program in the United States at the end of this month. The report describes the move as "one of the biggest changes ever to how the company sells devices."

Here's how it works.

Lower monthly payments for hardware purchases

Apple will partner with Klarna to support the new Apple Upgrade program. Consumers will need to undergo a soft credit check when applying.

According to reports, Apple Upgrade will operate "like a subscription service," applicable to purchases of iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple Watch. However, the program has certain restrictions. The report notes that Apple Watch SE, the basic iPad, iPhone 16 and MacBook Neo are not eligible for Apple Upgrade.

According to reports, the lease term for iPhone and Apple Watch is 24 months, while the lease term for Mac is 36 months.

Mark Gurman explains:

Unlike the iPhone Upgrade Program, Apple Upgrade does not include AppleCare coverage. In fact, Bloomberg notes that Apple plans to stop new enrollments for the iPhone Upgrade Program with the launch of Apple Upgrade.

According to reports, Apple Upgrade will officially launch one week from today, that is, on July 28.

Apple raised prices for iPad and Mac last month, and the new iPhone expected to launch in September is also projected to see a price increase. Apple Upgrade will provide customers with an option to cope with the price hikes.
